title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Divesting from Illegal Israeli Settlements) Bill 2024
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Divesting from Illegal Israeli Settlements) Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require the Future Fund and registered Australian charities to divest from, and stop investing in or supporting, companies on a United Nations (UN) database the bill describes as listing companies operating in illegal Israeli settlements on Palestinian land.
It would amend the Future Fund Act 2006 so the Board of Guardians must not invest in listed companies and must divest as soon as it becomes aware of such a holding.

Schedule 2 would extend the same restrictions to registered charities through the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 and the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission Act and Regulations, with a negligible expected budget impact.
changes: The Future Fund Act 2006 and charities regulations would define the bill's terms 'illegal Israeli settlements' and 'UN database', published under Human Rights Council resolution 31/36; the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 would define only the database.
The responsible Minister would have to consider the prohibition when giving investment directions under section 18 and could not direct the Board to invest in a listed company.
The Future Fund's annual report would have to include a statement of compliance confirming that no assets are invested in a listed company.
Registered charities could not use money or assets from their gift fund to fund, support or contribute to a listed company.
A new external conduct standard would direct registered charities not to fund, support, invest in or cooperate with listed companies or the settlements.
summary.affected: The Future Fund, registered Australian charities and companies listed on the UN database would be affected.
